newsitem.title: UKRAINE: SOCCER-DYNAMO KIEV IMPOSE "STATE OF EMERGENCY".
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DYNAMO KIEV IMPOSE "STATE OF EMERGENCY".

text.p: Ukraine's leading soccer club Dynamo Kiev has imposed a "state of emergency" giving its coach sweeping powers, including the right to cut salaries, after a series of dismal European matches.
A statement issued on Saturday by the club said management had given Dynamo's chief coach Yozhef Sabo carte blanche "to establish order and discipline".
Dynamo were knocked out in the qualifying round of the European Champions League last month after losing twice to Rapid Vienna.
This week, Dynamo could do no better than a 0-0 draw at home in front of 60,000 fans in the UEFA Cup to Switzerland's Xamax Neuchatel.
"There is lack of mutual understanding, a feeling of being out of touch with reality, an excess of self-confidence and a decline in discipline," the statement said.
"All forms of independence and autonomy are hereby cancelled and the principle of `single leadership' introduced."
Sabo was empowered to cut pay of players and other coaches and cancel bonuses. Players are even subject to dismissal.

The daily Kievskiye Vedomosti reported that Dymano had started secret negotiations with Valery Lobanovsky, former chief coach of both the Soviet squad and Dynamo Kiev. Lobanovsky currently trains Kuwait's national side.
Dynamo have won the Soviet championship 13 times, the Soviet cup nine times and the European Cup Winners' Cup twice.
UEFA allowed Dynamo back into competition after the club served one year of a three-year suspension for offering a bribe to a referee before a Champions' League match a year ago.

Club sources said Sabo was particulary unhappy about leading forward Viktor Leonenko. Last year Leonenko was demoted to Dynamo's second team after being accused by his coach of lack of discipline, gaining weight and excessive beer drinking.
